Epic: Canonical Incident Report Contract
Purpose: Define the first-class incident report contract for k9b beta so operators can understand an active situation quickly without stitching together multiple detailed panels.
Status: Implemented (see src/k8sdiagagent/ui/apiincidentreport.py, tests/unit/testapiincidentreport.py, tests/fixtures/incidentreportfixtures.py)
1. IncidentReportView Schema Definition
The canonical incident report contract is defined as IncidentReportPayload (Python TypedDict) and IncidentReportPayload (TypeScript) in the respective type definition files.
Every claim in the incident report is classified into one of five types:
| observed | Direct telemetry signal (metric, event count, status) | Must have sourceArtifactRefs |
| hypothesis | Plausible cause requiring confirmation | Must have non-empty basis |
| unknown | Explicitly acknowledged missing evidence | Must NOT be omitted or invented |
Each field in IncidentReportPayload maps to existing source artifacts:
| IncidentReport Field | Source Artifact | Mapping Logic |
| status | fleetstatus | "degraded" if any clusters in degradedclusters; "healthy" otherwise |
| facts[].sourceArtifactRefs | drilldowns/ artifactpath | Points to drilldown artifact |
| derived[].sourceArtifactRefs | assessments/ artifactpath | Points to assessment artifact |
| staleEvidenceWarnings | freshness.status | "Run freshness is {status}; some evidence may be stale." when status in ("delayed", "stale") |
Rule 1: Facts are deterministic/evidence-backed only
- Provider-assisted review enrichment summaries → inferences[] only
- Hypothesis descriptions → inferences[] only
- Missing evidence → unknowns[] only
- Never appears in facts[] regardless of content
- Unknowns are never omitted or converted to confident statements
- When freshness.status is "delayed" or "stale", staleEvidenceWarnings is populated
- Warning text: "Run freshness is {status}; some evidence may be stale."
Rule 5: Provider-assisted content is never classified as deterministic fact
Critical invariant: Review enrichment is always inferences[], never facts[]
Rule 6: Source artifact refs are preserved where available
- Each claim includes sourceArtifactRefs pointing to originating artifact
- Paths are real (from artifactpath fields), never "unknown"

- runs/snapshots/: sanitized Kubernetes snapshots collected during the run. Files keep deterministic snapshot metadata so the collector/compare CLI path keeps working unchanged.
- runs/assessments/: assessment payloads (matching docs/schemas/assessment-schema.md) produced during reasoning or LLM paths to keep track of expected outputs.
- Snapshot files are runs/snapshots/{context}-{timestamp}.json so collection flows can append data without breaking the deterministic CLI or fixture runner.
- Assessments are runs/assessments/{runid}-assessment.json and mirror the structure described in docs/schemas/assessment-schema.md.
- Feedback artifacts live in runs/feedback/{timestamp}-{runid}.json and conform to docs/schemas/feedback-artifact-schema.md.

- Health assessments are runs/health/assessments/{runid}-{cluster}.json and follow the same assessment schema. Each health artifact (assessments, comparisons, triggers) records the stable runlabel from the config while {runid} is the timestamped identifier generated for the current execution. Triggered comparisons land under runs/health/comparisons along with runs/health/triggers, and runs/health/history.json tracks the previous runs that inform heuristics.

- The existing deterministic collection/compare commands continue to serialize snapshots and diffs under runs/snapshots and runs/comparisons as before; feedback artifacts are additive and only read optional extra metadata.

- The k8s-diag-agent run-feedback command bridges collection, comparison, optional assessment, and validation so every execution writes a self-contained set of artifacts under this layout. Validators can replay a RunArtifact by reading the referenced snapshot, comparison, and assessment files, enabling evaluation and adaptation loops to rerun deterministically.
